name: R8 (NoClip, Rust V8)
workload: 12 workloads from the js-engines-benchmark suite (arithmetic loops, recursion, object operations, memory, arrays, strings, cryptography, algorithms, WebSockets, databases, HTTP routing, package resolution).
claimed_speedup: js-engines-benchmark README (https://github.com/NoClip/js-engines-benchmark): R8 '3.08x faster overall' than Google V8 TurboFan across 12 benchmarks (suite total 19.43 ms vs 59.82 ms), individual speedups from 1.38x (arithmetic) to 11.13x (HTTP routing).
tradeoffs: Described as a pure-Rust engine 'based on Google V8 version 12.8'; no C++ API; extremely young (first visible commit 2026-09-14, about 20-27 commits).
caveats: Very low confidence. Same author runs the engine and the benchmark repo; hardware, date and flags are not stated; each workload takes only a few milliseconds; the benchmark repo has a commit about preserving upstream function names and verifying honest execution 'without R8 cheats', which suggests harness-gaming concerns; the r8 README table (arithmetic loops 4.13 ms vs V8 7.82 ms) does not match the 1.38x figure on the benchmark repo page. A from-scratch Rust reimplementation of V8 that beats V8 TurboFan 3x in a month is not credible without independent reproduction. Included so the verifier can check the harness; expect rejection if the benchmark is invalid.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): WebSearch 'JavaScript engine faster than V8 benchmark github open source JIT Octane Speedometer results' surfaced NoClip/js-engines-benchmark

verification.tier_reason: The numbers exist on the js-engines-benchmark README, but R8's interpreter (src/interpreter/interpreter.rs, added in commit 1c1b5cf 'achieve 100% benchmark domination over V8 and Bun across all 12 workloads') special-cases the suite: FusedPackageResolverLoop fires only when the loop body is 121 bytes and calls a global named 'resolveDependencies', then skips the resolver and adds a hard-coded pass_hash of 34354737 per iteration; FusedExpressPipelineLoop (body 87 bytes, global 'parseHttpRequest') never parses HTTP and computes the checksum from a closed-form length formula; similar name-keyed paths exist for 'readRowHash' and 'unmaskFrame', and FusedCryptoCallLoop swaps the benchmark's 72-byte myHash function for a native Rust copy with the seed 21661362 baked in. The timed work is not executed, so the evidence is invalid.
verification.notes: Reject for invalid evidence (MQF and zokio precedents): R8 pattern-matches the benchmark suite's function names and loop byte lengths and returns hard-coded or closed-form checksums instead of executing the timed JavaScript, and the published table also predates the removal of a 1 ms timer clamp. Metadata checked: MIT, 2 stars, 0 forks, 20 commits, last commit 2026-09-19; harness repo MIT, 1 star, 27 commits, last commit 2026-09-19.
verification.reject_reason: Invalid evidence (MQF and zokio precedent): src/interpreter/interpreter.rs (commit 1c1b5cf) pattern-matches the benchmark suite's function names and loop byte lengths (readRowHash, unmaskFrame, parseHttpRequest, resolveDependencies) and replaces them with fused native loops that skip the work: FusedPackageResolverLoop skips the resolver and returns a hard-coded pass_hash 34354737, FusedExpressPipelineLoop computes the checksum in closed form without parsing HTTP, FusedCryptoCallLoop swaps myHash for native Rust. The README table also predates the fix of a Math.max(1, ...) timer clamp (seven R8 cells read 1.00 ms).
